rationale: B wins because it finds cleaner, more separate stories and is tougher about what cannot be pitched yet. Its "Klarna automated two-thirds of its chats. The other third got harder." is a genuinely different operations lens, while A's "Klarna's AI resolves disputes in under two minutes" smuggles a dispute claim into a generic support-speed metric. A has usable bones, but B is the one a founder could take into a real targeting meeting without stepping on its own numbers.
gaps_in_A: "Klarna's AI resolves disputes in under two minutes" is overclaiming. The update gives average customer-service resolution time, not dispute-resolution time or dispute accuracy.
"one of the only companies publishing operational numbers" is an unsupported comparative claim. Rare may be true, but it is not in the supplied facts.
The data angle and "How AI actually shrinks a company" overlap around the same 700-FTE/headcount story. They are adjacent, not fully separate.
"public markets pay a premium for AI head-count reduction" is a sharper markets question than the facts can support without filing language or investor evidence.
gaps_in_B: "The other third got harder" is a strong angle, but it is still an inference. The update does not say the remaining chats are harder, longer, or more stressful.
"the machine takes the two-thirds that were resolvable in minutes" overstates what "handles two-thirds" proves. Handled is not the same as easy, correct, or fully resolved.
"nobody publishes numbers on" is a broad unsourced claim. Useful color, but too sweeping without evidence.
"pull comparators and get a union or labour-economist voice" adds a union frame not present in the facts. Fine as reporting texture, weak as supplied grounding.
